Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Goal of the Game 2 Animal Cards 3 Ferries 4 Player Turn 4.1 Animal Card Placement 4.2 Moving the Noah Marker 5 Round End & Game End 6 Animals Cards and Special Effects 6.1 Standard Animals 6.2 Bonus Animals Goal of the Game Distribute animal cards from your hand onto the 5 ferries bound for Noah's Ark. A game is played over three rounds. Each round ends when either: One player has placed their last animal card onto a ferry, or four ferries have departed for the Ark. After three rounds, the winner is the player with the fewest Penalty Points (tear drops) at the end of the game. (Alternatively, game end is triggered if someone exceeds 26 Penalty Points.) Animal Cards Each player is dealt 8 animal cards each round. Animal cards display the following: Name: Name of the animal (see table below) Weight: From 0 to 10 Gender: BLUE for Male. PINK for Female. (The Snail card is a hermaphrodite and can be played as either Male or Female) Penalty Points: 0 to 5 "tear drops", reflecting Noah’s sadness at not being able to save the animal Noah's Movement Indicator: Male animals will move Noah "across and left" or "across and right". Female animals move Noah "left" or "right". Effect Icon: If the animal has one or more special effects (see table below) Ferries Each round starts with five ferries, each loaded with one random animal. When a ferry has been loaded with animals whose combined weight EXACTLY match the ferry's capacity, the ferry "departs" for the Ark. Player Turn On your turn you must: Play an animal card from your hand onto the ferry that the Noah marker is on. Move the Noah marker according to the played card's Movement Indicator. Animal Card Placement You must place one animal card from your hand onto the ferry where the Noah marker resides following these rules: Animal cards placed on a ferry either: Must be all the same gender (all Male or all Female), or Must alternate genders (MFMF... or FMFM...). Each ferry has a weight limit of 21 (unless modified by a Woodpecker card, which lowers the weight limit to 13). The weight of an animal placed on a ferry cannot exceed the ferry's remaining capacity. The ferry "departs" for the Ark when it reaches its EXACT weight limit. Then: The cards on the ferry are discarded. The player who "filled the ferry" gets to give away card(s) from their hand to their opponent(s): One card given per ferry that has departed this round (1, 2, 3, or 4). If you are unable to play a card (due to gender or weight restrictions) you must instead take ALL the cards from that ferry back into your hand. You then play a card from your hand onto that same (now-empty) ferry. Special Effect: Some animal cards provide a special effect when played (see list below). Extra Turn Bonus: If you play an animal card that matches the animal card below it (i.e.: has the same name , for example a 'Cat' card on 'Cat' card) you get to take another turn (after moving Noah). Note: Gender has no impact on achieving the Bonus. Placing either a Male or Female card on another Male or Female card with matching names will achieve the Bonus. Note: The Bonus can be achieved over and over again if your cards allow it. (Remember, you still must move Noah between your extra turns.) Note: The Bonus can be achieved multiple times even on the same ferry and even with repeated placement of the same animal. For example if, on a previous turn, a Cat card was placed on another Cat card, it is still legal to place another Cat card (making a stack of three Cat cards) to achieve the Bonus. ---

In Noah (Noé in the French original) the flood is at hand, and to save as many species as possible, Noah will need your help – with only the most deserving of players being saved from the waters!

Each round, players start with eight animal cards in hand; five ferries are laid out in a circle, with one animal placed on board from the top of the deck. Noah himself stands on one ferry. On a turn, a player plays one card from hand onto the ferry where Noah is located, following two rules: (1) the total weight of all animals on board cannot exceed 21 and (2) animals on a ferry must be placed either in alternating gender order or must be all of the same gender. After placing an animal, the player moves Noah to a different ferry; if he played a female animal, Noah goes to either adjacent ferry, while if he played a male, Noah goes to either ferry on the other side of the circle.

If a player can't legally play an animal, he must first take in hand all the animals on the ferry where Noah is located, then play an animal.

In addition to moving Noah to a nearly full ferry, players have two other ways to benefit themselves or mess with other players. If a player plays an animal of the same species as the one last played on that ferry (regardless of gender), he moves Noah, then takes another turn. If a player brings the weight of a ferry to exactly 21, that ferry launches from shore to meet the ark located in distant waters, a new ferry becomes available for loading, and the player distributes 1–4 cards from his hand among his opponents. finally, some cards have special animals, such as the giraffe that lets you peek at an opponent's hand and the woodpecker, which stupidly pokes holes in the ferry and reduces its maximum weight to 13. Bad woodpecker, bad!

The round ends when a player runs out of cards in hand or a fourth ferry launches. Players receive penalty points for cards still in hand, scored according to the number of tears on each card, those tears representing Noah's sadness at the animal being left behind. Then players shuffle all the animal cards and begin a new round. The player with the fewest points after three rounds wins!

[Rating: 1/10] Awful, no choices, this game plays itself. Only choices are basically random, no point in playing this game.

[Rating: 1/10] Almost no decisions and long for a game of this weight.  It is colourful and could work as a card game for young kids but there are many other games I'd recommend over this.

[Rating: 2/10] Tedius with almost no decisions, and yet despite that, there's way too much downtime, as well.

[Rating: 2/10] The game can go on forever and ever, lot of repetition, both which I don't enjoy much.

[Rating: 3/10] This felt a bit clunky for me. There are so many cards game out there that one needs to differentiate themselves from others to be remembered. This one achieved it, only in a bad way. Felt way too long for what it is.

[Rating: 3/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  I'd recommend not playing until someone hits 26 penalty points for your first game! ;-) Got repetitive pretty quickly playing a bunch of 21 games at the same time but with an opponent choosing which one.

[Rating: 3/10] This is barely even a game. It's just an exercise in laying cards. Massive yawn-fest.
